title: Firefox for iOS
description: Build a SwiftUI/WebKit browser-shell mini app with URL/search handling, tab state, protection settings, and rule-based tracking controls.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend Firefox for iOS while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace tab, protection-level, and tracker data types in its named source files.
Explain and trace url recognition, scheme normalization, and search fallback in its named source files.
Explain and trace representable wrapper, load calls, and browser controls in its named source files.
Explain and trace protection modes, rule selection, rule compilation, and observed count in its named source files.
Explain and trace observable store lifecycle, tab navigation, and settings binding in its named source files.
Explain and trace xctest assertions, target configuration, and what a test does not establish in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
